title: SLI surgeon runbook for token inference & dashboard triage
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational runbook for the SLI "surgeon" role to triage token-level inference regressions quickly. Focus is on fast signal localization (prefix/KV warmth, batching, model runtime), low-cost traces to capture root cause candidates, and dashboard probes that consistently reproduce the operator mental model.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to text-generation endpoints (hosted & dedicated) where token tail latency or p99/p999 regressions are observed.
- Assumes standard trace anchors are present on request_ingest, model_dispatch, kv_lookup, kernel_exec, and emit_token spans.
- This doc prioritizes signal that is inexpensive to fetch (dashboard widgets, short trace grabs, lightweight SQL) before requesting full trace dumps.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Validate the alert: check the SLI window, granularity, and recent modifications to SLI definition. Confirm whether the spike is localized to a route/model/customer cohort.
2) Check high-level panels: request-rate, p50/p90/p99 time-to-first-token, p99 token-generation-tail. Note whether only TTF token or generation tail is affected.
3) KV cache warmth: open the KV Warmth widget for affected model version + tenant. If warmth drops, suspect cold cache or eviction pressure.
4) Batching/utilization: check batch_utilization_ratio and queue_depth. Large batch growth with unchanged GPU utilization implies queuing.
5) Downstream resource signals: GPU utilization, PCIe stalls, and host CPU steal. If GPU utilization is 95%+ with normal queue depth, suspect kernel hotspots.
6) Short traces: sample 5 recent traces (1–2 spans per trace) anchored to the slowest requests. Look for repeated span (e.g., repeated kernel_exec retries or long kv_lookup).
7) Compare model variants: if model_swap_rate spiked (automatic fallbacks), routing may be forcing a heavier model.
8) If metrics point to cost/latency tradeoff changes (quantization toggles, new kernel selectors), check recent rollout notes and linked PRs.
9) Mitigate: if P0, shift routing to a faster model variant or enable fallback. If it's tenant-specific, throttle tenant or engage dedicated capacity.
10) Post-mortem stub: capture timestamps, topology snapshot, and one slow trace for later deep-dive.

Metric definitions (compact):
- request_ttf_ms: request to first-token in milliseconds (SLO anchored).
- token_tail_p99_ms: per-request p99 of total token generation time (ms).
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: ratio of successful prefix/KV fetches to total attempts (0–1).
- prefix_warmth_index: rolling-weighted indicator of recent prefix accesses (0–100).
- batch_utilization_ratio: observed batch size / configured max batch.
- model_swap_rate: number of requests re-routed to fallback model per minute.
- aborted_generation_rate: fraction of requests aborted due to runtime OOMs or preemption.
- inferred_token_cost_per_1k: cost estimate for tokens produced in the window.
- operator_investigation_score: internal heuristic combining SLI deviation, breadth (tenants affected), and repeat offenders (0–100).

Trace anchors and recommended span filters:
- request_ingest (tags: route, tenant, model, request_id)
- routing_decision (tags: policy, reason, fallback_model)
- kv_lookup (tags: prefix_hash, kv_shard, hit)
- kernel_exec (tags: gpu_id, batch_size, seq_len, kernel_variant)
- emit_token (tags: token_count, cost_estimate)

When grabbing traces, include span.duration, span.tags[kv_hit], and span.tags[kernel_variant]. Use adaptive sampling: 1% baseline, 10% when operator_investigation_score > 30. For a suspected KV-related event, prefer traces that contain kv_lookup spans and include prefix_hash.

Dashboard probes (fast widgets to check):
- Heatmap: token_tail_p99_ms by route x minute (30m window) -> quick visual of hotspots.
- Sparklines: kv_cache_hit_ratio for top 20 tenants in last 60m.
- Cohort timeline: request_ttf_ms p50/p99 split by tenant-weighted cohorts (internal/external).
- Queue vs GPU: batch_queue_depth vs GPU_utilization 1m aligned.
- Model rollouts: model_swap_rate and last_deployment_id overlay.
- Error composition: aborted_generation_rate broken down by OOM vs preemption vs internal_error.

Investigation recipes (targeted):
A) Cold-cache suspected:
  - Confirm: prefix_warmth_index drop coincident with p99 spike.
  - Quick check: synthetic probe replay for a small set of affected prefixes (non-prod tenant).
  - Short fix: increase prefetch budget for affected tenants or warm hotspots via async prefetch jobs.
  - Longer fix: evaluate KV TTL and eviction policy; consider tiered hot shards.

B) Batching-induced queuing:
  - Confirm: batch_utilization_ratio rises and queue_depth grows while GPU utilization is moderate.
  - Root: downstream queue config or mis-tuned autoscaler.
  - Quick fix: reduce max_batch_wait_ms or add workers to serving pool for the route.

C) Kernel/regression hotspot:
  - Confirm: GPU utilization spikes and kernel_exec spans show long durations or different kernel_variant.
  - Check: latest kernel-selector commit or model compile artifact.
  - Mitigation: force previous kernel variant, schedule emergency rollback of kernel selection artifact.

D) Routing/Model swap noise:
  - Confirm: model_swap_rate spikes and latency tracks with fallback model.
  - Mitigation: pin the route to the prior stable model version, adjust routing policies, throttle fallbacks.

Alert tuning guidance (avoid noisy false positives):
- Use multi-dimensional guards on alerts: combine token_tail_p99_ms with request_rate and kv_cache_hit_ratio so transient spikes during short traffic bursts don’t fire.
- Add a throttle window: require sustained deviation for 2 consecutive 5m buckets for non-P0 alerts.
- Alert severity mapping: P0 if > 5 tenants affected and request_ttf_ms > 4x baseline; P1 if single tenant or < 5% of global traffic.

Operator playbook: escalation and communication
- 0–10m: contain. Document immediate action, time, and temporary mitigations in Slack incident channel.
- 10–60m: stabilize. Identify candidate root cause, implement soft rollback or routing pin, gather traces and metrics for postmortem.
- 60m+: restore & review. If mitigated, schedule postmortem and assign CC. If not, escalate to infra/serving-runtime/ML infra owners depending on root cause.

Checklist for postmortem artifacts to capture:
- A single slow trace and a counterfactual fast trace.
- Dashboard snapshot (30m) and query ids.
- Top-10 impacted prefixes and tenanted delta.
- Associated deploys/PRs and autoscaler events.

Operator heuristics, notes to self (informal):
- For token-heavy prompts, be wary of seq_len skew; p99 may look fine but p999 reveals tail.
- Prefix warming sometimes lags dashboards; rely on synthetic warming probes where possible.
- In multi-tenant noise, checking the 95th tenant by volume often reveals a single noisy customer.
- If kernel variants flip between stable and experimental, gamma the toggle off immediately and capture compile metadata.

Outstanding questions / follow-ups:
- Can we add a low-cost probe that simulates prefix warming without using model capacity? (PRI: medium)
- How to better attribute cost impact to routing decisions for public dashboards? (PRI: low)
- Can we produce a single-lineage trace id that ties model compilation artifact -> kernel_variant -> runtime? (PRI: high)

Actions (next 30 days):
- Ship: lightweight warming probe prototype and integrate into dashboard (owner: Marco).
- Audit: SLI definitions across top 10 routes to align p99 windows and tag coverage (owner: Priya).
- Instrument: ensure kernel_variant tag is mandatory for kernel_exec spans (owner: Omar).

References and quick links:
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-1284: SLI taxonomy board (overview)
- JIRA-OP-3421: Runbook improvements epic
- Slack thread: #ops-triage (for live incidents)

If you are the on-call SLI surgeon: start with the checklist, capture one artifact every 15 minutes, and prefer conservative rollbacks over speculative config tweaks.
